pages.quiz:
ENGLISH ACTIVITIES — TERMLY EXAM #13
====

GRADE: Grade 1
SUBJECT: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. went
   B. goed
   C. goes
   D. going

2. When practising Handwriting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Handwriting.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Handwriting.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Handwriting.

3. When practising Phonics, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Phonics.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Phonics.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Phonics.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonics.

4. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Only one word repeated
   B. No full stops
   C. One main idea with supporting sentences
   D. Many unrelated topics with no link

5. When practising Language Welcome and, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Welcome and.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Language Welcome and.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Language Welcome and.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Language Welcome and.

6. When practising Pre-Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Pre-Writing.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-Writing.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Pre-Writing.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Pre-Writing.

7. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. Only a describing word
   C. Only an action
   D. A person, place, thing, or idea

8. When practising Word Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Word Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Word Reading.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Word Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.

9. When practising Pre Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Pre Reading.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Pre Reading.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Pre Reading.

10. When practising Connected text and fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Connected text and fluency.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Connected text and fluency.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Connected text and fluency.

11. When practising Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Comprehension.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Comprehension.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Comprehension.

12. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library
   B. Where is the Library
   C. where is the library
   D. Where is the library?

13. When practising Language School, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Language School.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Language School.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language School.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Language School.

14. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. run
   B. blue
   C. quickly
   D. happiness

15. When practising Attentive listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Attentive listening.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Attentive listening.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive listening.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Attentive listening.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Handwriting and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Punctuation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Attentive listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Language Welcome and and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Language School and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:

====

2. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.

3. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonics.

4. C — One main idea with supporting sentences

5. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Welcome and.

6. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-Writing.

7. D — A person, place, thing, or idea

8. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.

9. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre Reading.

10. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.

11. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.

12. D — Where is the library?

14. A — run

15. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive listening.

20. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Language Welcome and; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
